ruling.recommended_action: Refund the surge differential of $2.45 (1.3× − 1.0× applied to the surgeable subtotal of $8.18) to the rider's original payment method; no driver action as the notification-duty requirements were met.
ruling.reasoning:
The quote was locked at 1.0× (upfront_quote $10.02, surgeable_subtotal $8.77). The surge log shows the multiplier rising to 1.3× at 14:09:55, i.e. between quote and pickup (trip start 14:13:00), and the rider was notified in-app at 14:10:20 — before the trip began. The notification text states the new multiplier ("Fares are 1.3× higher right now"), a revised estimated fare ("Your new estimated fare is $12.65") and free cancellation ("You can cancel for free"). All three SURGE-1 items are present, so the rider WAS notified: under SURGE-2 the default row would be no_action.

However, the revised estimate the rider was given ($12.65) is not the fare charged ($11.88), and the difference is not driven solely by surge. The surgeable subtotal also shrank between quote ($8.77) and trip ($8.18, because the actual distance 2.43 km came in under the estimated 2.513 km), so the surge differential must be computed on the trip's own surgeable subtotal as SURGE-3 requires when causes are mixed: (1.3 − 1.0) × $8.18 = $2.45, which matches the recorded surge_amount of $2.45 (booking fee $1.25 is surge-exempt and excluded). The rider's complaint that the notified fare differed from the charged fare is made out only to this extent: the notice's $12.65 estimate overstated the true 1.3× fare by $0.77, which the rider has in fact already had the benefit of (she was charged $11.88, not $12.65). Refunding the full surge differential of $2.45 leaves the base, distance, time and booking-fee components payable.

No route deviation arises: actual distance 2.43 km is below the recommended 2.513 km, so the deviation is negative (RD-1 tolerance not exceeded) and no excess distance fare exists. The driver's statement that he "drove the route the app showed" is consistent with the telemetry. No safety indicators appear anywhere in the chat, complaint or driver statement.

element_findings.element: SURGE-1 notice: states the new surge multiplier
element_findings.reason: Notification text reads "Fares are 1.3× higher right now", expressly stating the 1.3× multiplier.

element_findings.element: SURGE-1 notice: states the revised estimated fare
element_findings.reason: Notification text reads "Your new estimated fare is $12.65".

element_findings.element: SURGE-1 notice: states the rider may cancel without penalty
element_findings.reason: Notification text reads "You can cancel for free" — a genuine free-cancel statement, not the qualified "cancellation fees may apply".

element_findings.element: SURGE-1 timing: notice before or at pickup / before trip start
element_findings.reason: Notice sent 14:10:20; trip started 14:13:00 — the notice preceded the trip.

element_findings.element: SURGE-3 basis: differential computed on trip surgeable subtotal (mixed causes)
element_findings.reason: Quote subtotal $8.77 vs trip subtotal $8.18 (actual distance below estimate), so the differential is (1.3−1.0)×$8.18 = $2.45, booking fee $1.25 excluded.

rejected_claims.reason: The rider was validly notified before departure: the in-app notice at 14:10:20 (before the 14:13:00 trip start) stated the new multiplier (1.3×), a revised estimated fare ($12.65) and free cancellation, satisfying SURGE-1. The notice therefore was not non-compliant as to the new multiplier or the free-cancel right; the only discrepancy is that the notified estimate ($12.65) was $0.77 higher than the fare actually charged ($11.88), and that excess was never collected from the rider. The refund is limited to the surge differential computed under SURGE-3.
